prov.text: The provision for credit losses increased by $8.5 million for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026 and decreased by $43.5 million for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the same periods in 2025. Provision expense for the nine-month period in 2025 included $62.0 million to establish an allowance for credit losses on the acquired loans designated as non-PCD loans at the close of the transaction. See Note 13, “Acquisition” above. The remainder of the increase in provision was driven by loan growth, general portfolio trends, and ongoing recalibrations of econometric loss models in the current period as compared to the prior periods. The Company’s nonperforming loans decreased $14.1 million to $117.9 million at September 30, 2026, compared to September 30, 2025. The ACL on loans as a percentage of total loans decreased to 1.06% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 1.07% at September 30, 2025. For a description of the Company’s methodology for computing the ACL, please see the summary discussion in the “Provision and Allowance for Credit Losses” section included below.

nonint.text: Noninterest expense decreased by $19.8 million, or 4.7%, for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, and decreased by $17.3 million, or 1.4%, for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same periods in 2025. These changes are discussed in greater detail below under Noninterest Expense.

nonop.text: Noninterest expense decreased by $19.8 million, or 4.7%, for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, and decreased by $17.3 million, or 1.4%, for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same periods in 2025. These changes are discussed in greater detail below under Noninterest Expense.

tax.text: The Company’s effective tax rate was 20.2% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 19.4% for the same period in 2025. The increase in the effective tax rate in 2026 is mainly due to more favorable discrete tax items in 2025, including a benefit from remeasuring deferred tax assets after the HTLF acquisition increased the state marginal tax rate. Additionally, a smaller proportion of pre-tax income in 2026 was earned from tax-exempt municipal securities.

net.text: For the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, Personal Banking net income improved $90.7 million, or 701.3%, to net income of $77.7 million, as compared to a net loss of $12.9 million in the same period in 2025. Net interest income increased $49.9 million, or 22.4%, compared to the same period in 2025 driven by organic loan growth, an additional month of activity from the acquisition of HTLF, and earning asset mix changes. Provision for credit losses decreased $15.8 million for the period, driven by the acquisition of HTLF as well as by portfolio metric changes and ongoing recalibrations of economic loss models in 2026 as compared to 2025. Noninterest income increased $20.8 million, or 16.2%, for the same period, primarily driven by increases of $14.5 million in investment securities gains, $5.1 million in trust and securities processing income, and $0.6 million in other income driven by increased life insurance income.

da.text: Occupancy expense increased $2.1 million, or 10.8%, and $5.8 million, or 10.7%, for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025, primarily due to increased depreciation expense related to assets acquired from the HTLF acquisition and increased building repair expense.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income is a significant source of the Company’s earnings and represents the amount by which interest income on earning assets exceeds the interest expense paid on liabilities. The volume of interest-earning assets and the related funding sources, the overall mix of these assets and liabilities, and the rates paid on each affect net interest income. Net interest income for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026 increased $65.0 million, or 13.7%, and increased $267.2 million, or 19.9%, compared to the same periods in 2025. The change in net interest income was primarily driven by favorable repricing of deposits in conjunction with lower short-term interest rates, and increases in average loans and average securities. These increases were partially offset by decreases in average interest-bearing due from banks and purchase accounting accretion income.

Table 1 shows the impact of earning asset rate changes compared to changes in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities. As illustrated in this table, net interest spread for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased 39 basis points as compared to the same period in 2025. Net interest margin for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased 28 basis points compared to the same period in 2025.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
A key objective of the Company is the growth of noninterest income to provide a diverse source of revenue not directly tied to interest rates. Fee-based services are typically non-credit related and are not generally affected by fluctuations in interest rates.

The Company offers multiple fee-based products and services, which management believes will more closely align with customer demands. The Company is currently emphasizing fee-based products and services including trust and securities processing, bankcard, securities trading and brokerage, and cash and treasury management. Management believes that it can offer these products and services both efficiently and profitably, as most have common platforms and support structures.

intro.text: UMB Financial Corporation (Nasdaq: UMBF) is a financial services company headquartered in Kansas City, Mo. UMB offers commercial banking, which includes comprehensive deposit, lending, investment and retirement plan services; personal banking, which includes comprehensive deposit, lending, wealth management and financial planning services; and institutional banking, which includes asset servicing, corporate trust solutions, investment banking and healthcare services. UMB operates branches throughout Missouri, Arizona, California, Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Illinois, Minnesota, Nebraska, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas, Utah, and Wisconsin. As the company’s reach continues to grow, it also serves business clients nationwide and institutional clients in several countries. For more information, visit UMB.com , UMB Blog , UMB Facebook and UMB LinkedIn .

s.t: The increase for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026 was driven by a $17.9 million gain on the sale of a security without readily determinable fair value and increases of $16.4 million in valuation of the Company’s securities without readily determinable fair value, both during 2026, offset by $20.9 million in net gains on the Company’s investment in Voyager Technologies, Inc. in 2025, which completed its initial public offering in June 2025.

On January 31, 2025 (Acquisition Date), the Company acquired all of the outstanding stock of Heartland Financial USA, Inc., a Delaware corporation (HTLF), in an all-stock transaction, issuing a total of 23.6 million shares of the Company’s common stock and 4.6 million depositary shares, each representing a 1/400th interest in a share of the Company’s 7.00 % Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series A (the Series A preferred stock).
